goal: Point the developer toward known Windows WebView2/Tauri resize performance causes and practical mitigations instead of profiling the tiny web page first.
must_include: Uses the Windows-only behavior, old WebView2 108, Tauri 1.2.x, and transparent borderless window as evidence that the shell/WebView resize path is suspect.
Recommends testing on current Tauri/WebView2 runtime versions because the source issue reports the behavior became much smoother with later WebView2/Tauri changes.
Suggests reducing or retesting transparent/window-effect/titlebar customizations on Windows because they can worsen resize/drag performance.
If offering the small resize-delay workaround, presents it as a temporary mitigation to validate the issue rather than as the preferred permanent fix.
must_not: Tell the developer to rewrite the frontend framework before checking the shell/WebView2 path.
Claim this is Linux-related when the fixture says Linux is smooth.
Recommend disabling hardware acceleration as the only solution without acknowledging WebView2/Tauri version and window-effect factors.
acceptable_alternatives: Create a minimal Tauri repro with and without transparency/decorations to isolate the window effect.
Compare against a current Tauri 2 project and the latest Evergreen WebView2 runtime before changing app UI code.
solved: The answer identifies the Windows Tauri/WebView2 resize path and gives update plus configuration/temporary mitigation steps.
partial: The answer says to profile resize performance but does not connect the symptoms to Tauri/WebView2/window transparency evidence.
notes: The issue ultimately closed after later WebView2/Tauri behavior improved; older Tauri 1.x projects may still need configuration workarounds.
